claim: Rat brain metabolism is reconfigured to achieve long-distance connections with higher energy efficiency during maturation.
source: Here, we show that rat brain metabolism is reconfigured to achieve long-distance connections with higher energy efficiency during maturation.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript including metabolic connectivity analyses and energy efficiency measurements.

claim: Metabolism increased in anterior cerebrum during maturation.
source: Metabolism increased in anterior cerebrum and decreased in thalamus and cerebellum during maturation.
evidence: Supported by voxelwise comparison data shown in Figure 1 and described in the Results section.

claim: Metabolism decreased in thalamus and cerebellum during maturation.
source: Metabolism increased in anterior cerebrum and decreased in thalamus and cerebellum during maturation.
evidence: Supported by voxelwise comparison data shown in Figure 1 and described in the Results section.

claim: Metabolic networks including default mode network (DMN) were extracted when functional covariance patterns of PET images were examined.
source: When functional covariance patterns of PET images were examined, metabolic networks including default mode network (DMN) were extracted.
evidence: Supported by ICA analysis results shown in Figure 2 and described in the Results section.

claim: Connectivity increased between the anterior and posterior parts of DMN during maturation.
source: Connectivity increased between the anterior and posterior parts of DMN and sensory-motor cortices during maturation.
evidence: Supported by connectivity analysis data shown in Figure 3 and described in the Results section.

claim: Connectivity increased between DMN and sensory-motor cortices during maturation.
source: Connectivity increased between the anterior and posterior parts of DMN and sensory-motor cortices during maturation.
evidence: Supported by connectivity analysis data shown in Figure 3 and described in the Results section.

claim: Energy efficiency increased in medial prefrontal cortices during maturation.
source: Energy efficiency, a ratio of connectivity strength to metabolism of a region, increased in medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices.
evidence: Supported by energy efficiency analysis data shown in Figure 4 and described in the Results section.

claim: Energy efficiency increased in retrosplenial cortices during maturation.
source: Energy efficiency, a ratio of connectivity strength to metabolism of a region, increased in medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices.
evidence: Supported by energy efficiency analysis data shown in Figure 4 and described in the Results section.

claim: Metabolic networks mature to increase metabolic connections between large-scale spatial components from childhood to early adulthood.
source: Our data revealed that metabolic networks mature to increase metabolic connections and establish its efficiency between large-scale spatial components from childhood to early adulthood.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the combined results of connectivity and efficiency analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Neurodevelopmental diseases might be understood by abnormal reconfiguration of metabolic connectivity and efficiency.
source: Neurodevelopmental diseases might be understood by abnormal reconfiguration of metabolic connectivity and efficiency.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential implications of the findings for understanding disease.

claim: Neuroimaging has been used to examine developmental changes of the brain.
source: Neuroimaging has been used to examine developmental changes of the brain.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, as indicated by the context and subsequent citations.

claim: PET studies revealed maturation-related changes in the brain.
source: While PET studies revealed maturation-related changes, maturation of metabolic connectivity of the brain is not yet understood.
evidence: This refers to existing literature on PET studies of brain maturation.

claim: Maturation of metabolic connectivity of the brain is not yet understood.
source: While PET studies revealed maturation-related changes, maturation of metabolic connectivity of the brain is not yet understood.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the current study addresses.

claim: Recent neuroimaging studies unraveled the developmental changes of the adolescent brains.
source: Recent neuroimaging studies unraveled the developmental changes of the adolescent brains (Blakemore, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Blakemore, 2012.

claim: Positron emission tomography (PET) provides quantitative information regarding regional metabolism or synaptic neurochemicals with high sensitivity.
source: Among those neuroimaging techniques, positron emission tomography (PET) provides quantitative information regarding regional metabolism or synaptic neurochemicals with high sensitivity.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PET imaging capabilities.

claim: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) is taken up in the brain proportional to cerebral energy consumption and neuronal activity.
source: As 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) is taken up in the brain proportional to cerebral energy consumption and neuronal activity, FDG PET studies have been used to investigate regional energy metabolism during physiologic and pathologic processes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FDG uptake mechanism.

claim: FDG PET studies have been used to investigate regional energy metabolism during physiologic and pathologic processes.
source: As 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) is taken up in the brain proportional to cerebral energy consumption and neuronal activity, FDG PET studies have been used to investigate regional energy metabolism during physiologic and pathologic processes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the application of FDG PET.

claim: Previous brain developmental studies using FDG PET in humans assumed that the regional increase of metabolism was accompanied by regional increase of neuronal activity during brain maturation.
source: Previous brain developmental studies using FDG PET in humans assumed that the regional increase of metabolism was accompanied by regional increase of neuronal activity during brain maturation (Chugani et al., 1987; Phelps and Mazziotta, 1985).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Chugani et al., 1987 and Phelps and Mazziotta, 1985.

claim: The developmental changes are not understood in terms of dynamic organization of metabolic networks between brain regions.
source: Despite these previous data, the developmental changes are not understood in terms of dynamic organization of metabolic networks between brain regions.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: A series of regional brain activity is being coherently organized changing throughout time.
source: Since a series of regional brain activity is being coherently organized changing throughout time, sets of specific brain regions are activated or deactivated during resting or various cognitive tasks.
evidence: This is established knowledge about brain network organization.

claim: Sets of specific brain regions are activated or deactivated during resting or various cognitive tasks.
source: Since a series of regional brain activity is being coherently organized changing throughout time, sets of specific brain regions are activated or deactivated during resting or various cognitive tasks.
evidence: This is established knowledge about brain network function.

claim: Functional brain networks are identified by neuroimaging studies.
source: These specific regional activity patterns, so-called functional brain networks, are identified by neuroimaging studies (Deco et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Deco et al., 2011.

claim: Resting state functional magnetic resonance image (fMRI)-based connectivity analyses revealed maturation of the functional networks during childhood and adolescence.
source: Among several imaging approaches, resting state functional magnetic resonance image (fMRI)-based connectivity analyses revealed maturation of the functional networks during childhood and adolescence (Fair et al., 2008; Fair et al., 2007; Supekar et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fair et al., 2008; Fair et al., 2007; Supekar et al., 2009.

claim: FDG PET can reveal functional metabolic network and its maturation, exploiting the coupling between neuronal activity and metabolism.
source: FDG PET can also reveal functional metabolic network and its maturation, exploiting the coupling between neuronal activity and metabolism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known properties of FDG PET and neurovascular coupling.

claim: fMRI-based functional connectivity measures correlation of fast temporal fluctuations.
source: While the fMRI-based functional connectivity measures correlation of fast temporal fluctuations, metabolic connectivity measured by FDG PET reflects a cumulative energy consumption in several minutes and provides relatively stable information regarding steady resting state (Choi et al., 2014; Di et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2012; Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge about fMRI.

claim: Metabolic connectivity measured by FDG PET reflects a cumulative energy consumption in several minutes and provides relatively stable information regarding steady resting state.
source: While the fMRI-based functional connectivity measures correlation of fast temporal fluctuations, metabolic connectivity measured by FDG PET reflects a cumulative energy consumption in several minutes and provides relatively stable information regarding steady resting state (Choi et al., 2014; Di et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2012; Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Choi et al., 2014; Di et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2012; Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013.

claim: FDG PET measures metabolic activity and connection patterns during awaken states even in animals as in humans, because FDG is taken up in the brain mainly during the period after injection and before the imaging under anesthesia.
source: Furthermore, FDG PET measures metabolic activity and connection patterns during awaken states even in animals as in humans, because FDG is taken up in the brain mainly during the period after injection and before the imaging under anesthesia.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of FDG uptake kinetics and the experimental protocol used.

claim: The brain needs efficient energy metabolism to organize highly connected functional brain networks.
source: To organize highly connected functional brain networks, which can be measured by fMRI or FDG PET, the brain needs efficient energy metabolism (Bullmore and Sporns, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Bullmore and Sporns, 2012.

claim: High energetic costs are required for brain wiring to construct and maintain hub regions with dense connections.
source: As the high energetic costs are required for brain wiring to construct and maintain hub regions with dense connections, hub regions will show high glucose metabolism (Lord et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Lord et al., 2013.

claim: Hub regions will show high glucose metabolism.
source: As the high energetic costs are required for brain wiring to construct and maintain hub regions with dense connections, hub regions will show high glucose metabolism (Lord et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between connectivity and metabolic cost, supported by citation to Lord et al., 2013.

claim: Brain regions show different regional energy efficiency.
source: Brain regions were found to show different regional energy efficiency so that, for instance, subcortical regions consumed relatively lower metabolic energy per connection (Tomasi et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Tomasi et al., 2013.

claim: Subcortical regions consumed relatively lower metabolic energy per connection.
source: Brain regions were found to show different regional energy efficiency so that, for instance, subcortical regions consumed relatively lower metabolic energy per connection (Tomasi et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Tomasi et al., 2013.

claim: Metabolism of brain regions could be determined both by the regional complexity of functional networks and their energy efficiency for wiring.
source: Therefore, we can say that metabolism of brain regions could be determined both by the regional complexity of functional networks and their energy efficiency for wiring.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between network complexity, energy efficiency, and metabolism.

claim: The developmental changes in functional networks reconfigure the metabolic demands.
source: Since the developmental changes in functional networks reconfigure the metabolic demands, energy efficiency of the brain networks are going to be changed during maturation.
evidence: This is an inference about the relationship between network development and metabolic demands.

claim: Energy efficiency of the brain networks are going to be changed during maturation.
source: Since the developmental changes in functional networks reconfigure the metabolic demands, energy efficiency of the brain networks are going to be changed during maturation.
evidence: This is an inference that forms part of the study's hypothesis.

claim: Animals allow repeated imaging studies.
source: As the animals allow repeated imaging studies, we could study longitudinal maturation of regional metabolism and connectivity in the same animals.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the advantages of animal studies.

claim: Small animals have default mode network (DMN).
source: As the small animals also have default mode network (DMN) (Lu et al., 2012) defined as brain regions activating during resting state and deactivating during attention-demanding tasks (Raichle et al., 2001), specific network components were extracted in the rat brain from minutes-scale metabolic covariance patterns and independent component analysis (ICA).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2012.

claim: DMN is defined as brain regions activating during resting state and deactivating during attention-demanding tasks.
source: As the small animals also have default mode network (DMN) (Lu et al., 2012) defined as brain regions activating during resting state and deactivating during attention-demanding tasks (Raichle et al., 2001), specific network components were extracted in the rat brain from minutes-scale metabolic covariance patterns and independent component analysis (ICA).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Raichle et al., 2001.

claim: Specific network components were extracted in the rat brain from minutes-scale metabolic covariance patterns and independent component analysis (ICA).
source: As the small animals also have default mode network (DMN) (Lu et al., 2012) defined as brain regions activating during resting state and deactivating during attention-demanding tasks (Raichle et al., 2001), specific network components were extracted in the rat brain from minutes-scale metabolic covariance patterns and independent component analysis (ICA).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The metabolic networks are dynamically organized during maturation to achieve connection efficiency.
source: We hypothesized the metabolic networks are dynamically organized during maturation to achieve connection efficiency.
evidence: This is the stated hypothesis of the study.

claim: The metabolism increased in 10-week-old age in bilateral frontal cortices and anterior aspect of striatum compared with 5-week-old age.
source: The comparison using statistical parametric mapping revealed that the metabolism increased in 10-week-old age in bilateral frontal cortices and anterior aspect of striatum compared with 5-week-old age and decreased in bilateral cerebellar cortices, thalamus, parieto-occipital cortices, and retrosplenial cortices (Figure 1A) (representative FDG PET images for each age are shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical parametric mapping results shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The metabolism decreased in 10-week-old age in bilateral cerebellar cortices, thalamus, parieto-occipital cortices, and retrosplenial cortices compared with 5-week-old age.
source: The comparison using statistical parametric mapping revealed that the metabolism increased in 10-week-old age in bilateral frontal cortices and anterior aspect of striatum compared with 5-week-old age and decreased in bilateral cerebellar cortices, thalamus, parieto-occipital cortices, and retrosplenial cortices (Figure 1A) (representative FDG PET images for each age are shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical parametric mapping results shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Metabolism increased in 15-week-old age compared with 10-week-old age, in the clusters of both hippocampi.
source: Again, metabolism increased in 15-week-old age compared with 10-week-old age, in the clusters of both hippocampi and decreased in the small clusters of right striatum and left frontal cortex (Figure 1B, Figure1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by statistical parametric mapping results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Metabolism decreased in 15-week-old age compared with 10-week-old age in the small clusters of right striatum and left frontal cortex.
source: Again, metabolism increased in 15-week-old age compared with 10-week-old age, in the clusters of both hippocampi and decreased in the small clusters of right striatum and left frontal cortex (Figure 1B, Figure1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by statistical parametric mapping results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Considerable metabolic maturation in frontal cortices occurs between 5 and 10 weeks, i.e. during adolescence.
source: The finding implies that considerable metabolic maturation in frontal cortices occurs between 5 and 10 weeks, i.e. during adolescence.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Visual inspection can detect increase of metabolism in anterior part of the brain during maturation concordant with the results of voxelwise comparison.
source: Visual inspection can detect increase of metabolism in anterior part of the brain during maturation concordant with the results of voxelwise comparison.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The patterns of increase and decrease of metabolism were similar to the comparison between 5-week and 10-week-old rats.
source: The patterns of increase and decrease of metabolism were similar to the comparison between 5-week and 10-week-old rats.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Metabolic maturation in the brain occurs before 10 weeks and almost reaches plateau.
source: The findings imply that metabolic maturation in the brain occurs before 10 weeks and almost reaches plateau.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: A total of 13 metabolic independent components (ICs) were identified in rats similar to components found in previous reports in humans on FDG PET.
source: A total of 13 metabolic independent components (ICs) were identified in rats similar to components found in previous reports in humans on FDG PET (Di et al., 2012; Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by ICA results and citations to Di et al., 2012; Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013.

claim: IC1 included the clusters of dorsal hippocampi and medial prefrontal cortex.
source: IC1 included the clusters of dorsal hippocampi and medial prefrontal cortex.
evidence: This is supported by ICA results shown in Figure 2.

claim: IC5 included the retrosplenial cortex, known as a hub of posterior DMN in rats.
source: IC5 included the retrosplenial cortex, known as a hub of posterior DMN in rats (Lu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by ICA results shown in Figure 2 and citation to Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Retrosplenial cortex is anatomically adjacent to the posterior cingulate and precuneus in human as cores of DMN.
source: It is anatomically adjacent to the posterior cingulate and precuneus in human as cores of DMN (Raichle et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Raichle et al., 2001 and represents anatomical knowledge.

claim: Eight VOIs (3 for IC1, 1 for IC5, 2 for IC8 and IC9, respectively) were selected taking anatomical structures into consideration.
source: Eight VOIs (3 for IC1, 1 for IC5, 2 for IC8 and IC9, respectively) were selected taking anatomical structures into consideration (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (stereotaxic coordinates and abbreviations of VOIs are summarized in Table 1).
evidence: This describes the methodology for VOI selection, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Table 1.

claim: The connection between pairs of retrosplenial, medial prefrontal, and sensorimotor cortices was strengthened from 5 to 10 weeks.
source: Connectivity matrices (Figure 3A) and p-values for the difference in connection strength (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) between paired groups suggested that the connection between pairs of retrosplenial, medial prefrontal, and sensorimotor cortices was strengthened from 5 to 10 weeks, while connectivity involving limbic regions did not change.
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Connectivity involving limbic regions did not change from 5 to 10 weeks.
source: Connectivity matrices (Figure 3A) and p-values for the difference in connection strength (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) between paired groups suggested that the connection between pairs of retrosplenial, medial prefrontal, and sensorimotor cortices was strengthened from 5 to 10 weeks, while connectivity involving limbic regions did not change.
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pairs of anterior-posterior connections were significantly strengthened when comparing 10-week-old rats with 5-week-old rats.
source: According to aging, pairs of anterior-posterior connections were significantly strengthened when comparing 10-week-old rats with 5-week-old rats (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The increase in anterior-posterior connectivity became prominent when comparing 15-week-old rats from 5-week-old rats.
source: The increase became prominent when we compared 15-week-old rats from 5-week-old rats.
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Connectivity was not significantly weakened between areas during maturation.
source: Connectivity was not significantly weakened between areas during maturation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In 5-week-old rats, energy efficiency was relatively lower in midline structures, that is, medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices than sensorimotor cortices.
source: In 5-week-old rats, energy efficiency was relatively lower in midline structures, that is, medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices than sensorimotor cortices.
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: In 10- and 15-week-old age compared with 5-week-old age, energy efficiency of the midline structures significantly increased almost reaching those of the sensorimotor cortices.
source: In 10- and 15-week-old age compared with 5-week-old age, energy efficiency of the midline structures significantly increased almost reaching those of the sensorimotor cortices (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: Large-scale brain network based on glucose metabolic usage measured by PET was analyzed to evaluate the maturation of the metabolic brain connectivity in rats.
source: In the present study, large-scale brain network based on glucose metabolic usage measured by PET was analyzed to evaluate the maturation of the metabolic brain connectivity in rats.
evidence: This describes the overall approach of the study.

claim: In adolescent (10 weeks) and early-adult (15 weeks) period, metabolism increased in the bilateral frontal lobes compared to childhood (5 weeks).
source: In adolescent (10 weeks) and early-adult (15 weeks) period, metabolism increased in the bilateral frontal lobes compared to childhood (5 weeks), whereas metabolism decreased in the posterior cerebrum, thalamus, and cerebellum.
evidence: This is supported by voxelwise comparison results shown in Figure 1.

claim: In adolescent (10 weeks) and early-adult (15 weeks) period, metabolism decreased in the posterior cerebrum, thalamus, and cerebellum compared to childhood (5 weeks).
source: In adolescent (10 weeks) and early-adult (15 weeks) period, metabolism increased in the bilateral frontal lobes compared to childhood (5 weeks), whereas metabolism decreased in the posterior cerebrum, thalamus, and cerebellum.
evidence: This is supported by voxelwise comparison results shown in Figure 1.

claim: Metabolic network components extracted using ICA were default-mode, limbic, motor, and somatosensory ones, which have been regarded as important functional components also in humans.
source: Metabolic network components extracted using ICA were default-mode, limbic, motor, and somatosensory ones, which have been regarded as important functional components also in humans.
evidence: This is supported by ICA results shown in Figure 2 and comparison with human literature.

claim: Connection strength increased particularly in the anterior-posterior connections during maturation.
source: Further connectivity analyses using VOIs put on these components showed connection strength increased particularly in the anterior-posterior connections during maturation.
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Connection strength increase was accompanied by increased energy efficiency in the midline structures including medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices.
source: This connection strength increase was accompanied by increased energy efficiency in the midline structures including medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortices.
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: Large-scale functional networks matured to increase anterior-posterior long-distance connections and achieved energetically efficient wiring in the midline structures during maturation from childhood via adolescence to early adulthood.
source: Our work suggested large-scale functional networks matured to increase anterior-posterior long-distance connections and achieved energetically efficient wiring in the midline structures during maturation from childhood via adolescence to early adulthood.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the combined results of the study.

claim: A study using 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT showed perfusion increase in the neocortex at juvenile to young adult periods in mice, particularly in frontal lobes relative to the cerebellum and subcortical structures.
source: A study using 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT showed perfusion increase in the neocortex at juvenile to young adult periods in mice, particularly in frontal lobes relative to the cerebellum and subcortical structures (Apostolova et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Apostolova et al., 2012.

claim: In humans, perfusion was lower in the neonates' neocortex while higher in the basal ganglia and cerebellum.
source: In humans, perfusion was lower in the neonates' neocortex while higher in the basal ganglia and cerebellum (Fockele et al., 1990).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Fockele et al., 1990.

claim: Positive correlation was found between age and frontal lobe perfusion.
source: Additionally, positive correlation was found between age and frontal lobe perfusion (Kuji et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Kuji et al., 1999.

claim: FDG PET studies in human showed significantly higher metabolism mostly in anterior cingulate and thalamus before 25-year-old.
source: FDG PET studies in human showed significantly higher metabolism mostly in anterior cingulate and thalamus before 25-year-old (Van Bogaert et al., 1998) and linear metabolism increase from the age of 115 in prefrontal/orbitofrontal cortices (Kang et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Van Bogaert et al., 1998.

claim: FDG PET studies in human showed linear metabolism increase from the age of 1-15 in prefrontal/orbitofrontal cortices.
source: FDG PET studies in human showed significantly higher metabolism mostly in anterior cingulate and thalamus before 25-year-old (Van Bogaert et al., 1998) and linear metabolism increase from the age of 115 in prefrontal/orbitofrontal cortices (Kang et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Kang et al., 2004.

claim: The findings of age-related frontal metabolism increase corresponded to human PET findings as well as perfusion studies in rodents.
source: As a first study in terms of longitudinal age-related brain metabolism in rats, our findings of age-related frontal metabolism increase corresponded to human PET findings as well as perfusion studies in rodents.
evidence: This is an inference comparing the current study's results with previous literature.

claim: Analysis of metabolic network are based on the sequential coupling of neuronal activity, brain metabolism, and blood flow, which more closely represent the neuronal networks than blood flow networks.
source: Analysis of metabolic network are based on the sequential coupling of neuronal activity, brain metabolism, and blood flow, which more closely represent the neuronal networks than blood flow networks.
evidence: This is an inference about the relationship between metabolic networks and neuronal networks.

claim: Metabolic activity measured by FDG uptake reflects the cumulative energy consumption in steady states.
source: Because metabolic activity measured by FDG uptake reflects the cumulative energy consumption in steady states, while BOLD signal from fMRI reflects fast temporal fluctuation of physiologic factors such as blood flow, blood oxygenation, and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen, the metabolic network provides distinct information from the functional network on fMRI as well as from the structural network disclosed on diffusion tensor imaging (Di et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FDG uptake, supported by citations.

claim: BOLD signal from fMRI reflects fast temporal fluctuation of physiologic factors such as blood flow, blood oxygenation, and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen.
source: Because metabolic activity measured by FDG uptake reflects the cumulative energy consumption in steady states, while BOLD signal from fMRI reflects fast temporal fluctuation of physiologic factors such as blood flow, blood oxygenation, and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen, the metabolic network provides distinct information from the functional network on fMRI as well as from the structural network disclosed on diffusion tensor imaging (Di et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about fMRI BOLD signal.

claim: The metabolic network provides distinct information from the functional network on fMRI as well as from the structural network disclosed on diffusion tensor imaging.
source: Because metabolic activity measured by FDG uptake reflects the cumulative energy consumption in steady states, while BOLD signal from fMRI reflects fast temporal fluctuation of physiologic factors such as blood flow, blood oxygenation, and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen, the metabolic network provides distinct information from the functional network on fMRI as well as from the structural network disclosed on diffusion tensor imaging (Di et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Di et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013.

claim: Network construction using neuronal activity-coupled metabolism found on FDG PET could take regional metabolic activities into account to disclose energy efficiency.
source: Furthermore, network construction using neuronal activity-coupled metabolism found on FDG PET could take regional metabolic activities into account to disclose energy efficiency rather than only concentrate on the changes of fluctuating neural activities without considering absolute amount of regional perfusion or metabolism (Hyder et al., 2011; Smith et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hyder et al., 2011; Smith et al., 2002.

claim: ICA for metabolic networks revealed DMN successfully in human brains.
source: In human brains, ICA for metabolic networks revealed DMN successfully (Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013.

claim: Homologous patterns in rats to those of humans were found using ICA.
source: We also found homologous patterns in rats to those of humans.
evidence: This is supported by ICA results shown in Figure 2.

claim: Each DMN from fMRI and PET shared quite the similar anatomical regions, although distinctive patterns were found on these two modalities.
source: According to the studies comparing the networks acquired from fMRI and PET, each DMN from these modalities shared quite the similar anatomical regions, although distinctive patterns were found on these two modalities (Di et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Di et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013.

claim: PET-derived IC5 shared the regions of fMRI-derived DMN including retrosplenial cortices and small clusters of bilateral posterior hippocampi.
source: Of note, our PET-derived IC5 shared the regions of fMRI-derived DMN including retrosplenial cortices and small clusters of bilateral posterior hippocampi.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study's results and previous fMRI studies.

claim: IC1 shared the regions of anterior part of DMN derived from fMRI, medial frontal cortices.
source: The IC1 shared the regions of anterior part of DMN derived from fMRI, medial frontal cortices (Lu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study's results and previous fMRI studies, supported by citation to Lu et al., 2012.

claim: DMN-related regions are deactivated during attention-demanding and working memory tasks.
source: Considering that DMN-related regions are deactivated during attention-demanding and working memory tasks (Raichle et al., 2001), DMN may be constructed during brain maturation in adolescence to learn attention-demanding tasks.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Raichle et al., 2001.

claim: DMN may be constructed during brain maturation in adolescence to learn attention-demanding tasks.
source: Considering that DMN-related regions are deactivated during attention-demanding and working memory tasks (Raichle et al., 2001), DMN may be constructed during brain maturation in adolescence to learn attention-demanding tasks.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the known function of DMN and the study's findings.

claim: Previous human studies on the fMRI-derived functional networks revealed connectivity increase in DMN regions during maturation, particularly between the anterior and posterior midline structures.
source: Previous human studies on the fMRI-derived functional networks revealed connectivity increase in DMN regions during maturation, particularly between the anterior and posterior midline structures (Fair et al., 2008), which might be closely associated with the developmental process of working memory (Satterthwaite et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fair et al., 2008 and Satterthwaite et al., 2013.

claim: Connectivity increase in DMN regions during maturation might be closely associated with the developmental process of working memory.
source: Previous human studies on the fMRI-derived functional networks revealed connectivity increase in DMN regions during maturation, particularly between the anterior and posterior midline structures (Fair et al., 2008), which might be closely associated with the developmental process of working memory (Satterthwaite et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Satterthwaite et al., 2013.

claim: fMRI-derived DMN showed two distinctive clusters, temporal-prefrontal and parietal subsystems, which considerably corresponded to IC1 and IC5.
source: Moreover, fMRI-derived DMN showed two distinctive clusters, temporal-prefrontal and parietal subsystems, which considerably corresponded to our IC1 and IC5 (Lu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study's results and previous fMRI studies, supported by citation to Lu et al., 2012.

claim: The metabolic connections of the two clusters of DMN developed during brain maturation in rats.
source: According to our results, the metabolic connections of these two clusters of DMN developed during brain maturation in rats.
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Metabolic networks derived from FDG PET were partly different from fMRI-derived networks.
source: In spite of homologous network patterns of rat brain, metabolic networks derived from FDG PET were partly different from fMRI-derived networks.
evidence: This is an observation based on comparison with previous fMRI studies.

claim: A discrepancy in DMN between fMRI and PET was also reported in human.
source: A discrepancy in DMN between fMRI and PET was also reported in human (Di et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Di et al., 2012.

claim: In PET-derived networks in the rat brain, anterior and posterior part of DMN was separately extracted (IC1 and IC5).
source: In PET-derived networks in the rat brain, anterior and posterior part of DMN was separately extracted (IC1 and IC5).
evidence: This is supported by ICA results shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cingulate cortex was rarely included in IC1 or IC5, which was different from previous fMRI-derived DMN.
source: Furthermore, cingulate cortex was rarely included in IC1 or IC5, which was different from previous fMRI-derived DMN (Lu et al., 2012; Sierakowiak et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an observation based on comparison with previous fMRI studies, supported by citations to Lu et al., 2012; Sierakowiak et al., 2015.

claim: A hub region of posterior part of rat DMN was retrosplenial cortex in fMRI study.
source: Nevertheless, a hub region of posterior part of rat DMN was retrosplenial cortex and that of anterior part was medial prefrontal cortex in fMRI study, which corresponded to PET-derived IC5 and IC1, respectively.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous fMRI studies.

claim: A hub region of anterior part of rat DMN was medial prefrontal cortex in fMRI study.
source: Nevertheless, a hub region of posterior part of rat DMN was retrosplenial cortex and that of anterior part was medial prefrontal cortex in fMRI study, which corresponded to PET-derived IC5 and IC1, respectively.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous fMRI studies.

claim: The hub regions in fMRI study corresponded to PET-derived IC5 and IC1, respectively.
source: Nevertheless, a hub region of posterior part of rat DMN was retrosplenial cortex and that of anterior part was medial prefrontal cortex in fMRI study, which corresponded to PET-derived IC5 and IC1, respectively.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study's results and previous fMRI studies.

claim: During connectivity maturation, metabolic connections between component VOIs strengthened, particularly in anterior-posterior long-distance ones.
source: During connectivity maturation, metabolic connections between component VOIs strengthened, particularly in anterior-posterior long-distance ones.
evidence: This is supported by connectivity analysis results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Along with increased long-distance connections, the retrosplenial and medial prefrontal cortices showed efficient energy consumption.
source: Along with increased long-distance connections, the retrosplenial and medial prefrontal cortices showed efficient energy consumption.
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: This maturation pattern may represent enhancement of efficiency of information flow between network components.
source: This maturation pattern may represent enhancement of efficiency of information flow between network components, which has been suggested in human brain maturation (Fair et al., 2007; Stevens et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of the findings, supported by citations to Fair et al., 2007; Stevens et al., 2009.

claim: Enhancement of efficiency of information flow between network components has been suggested in human brain maturation.
source: This maturation pattern may represent enhancement of efficiency of information flow between network components, which has been suggested in human brain maturation (Fair et al., 2007; Stevens et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fair et al., 2007; Stevens et al., 2009.

claim: The strengthened connections between long-distance network components are likely to support dynamically organizing brain networks to achieve efficient connections according to cognitive demands.
source: The strengthened connections between long-distance network components are likely to support dynamically organizing brain networks to achieve efficient connections according to cognitive demands (Bullmore and Sporns, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of the findings, supported by citation to Bullmore and Sporns, 2012.

claim: The functional interactions of large-scale brain networks are dynamically evolving.
source: The functional interactions of large-scale brain networks are dynamically evolving, which could be associated with cognitive, behavioral developments during maturation and pathophysiology of brain disorders (Deco et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Deco et al., 2011.

claim: The functional interactions of large-scale brain networks could be associated with cognitive, behavioral developments during maturation and pathophysiology of brain disorders.
source: The functional interactions of large-scale brain networks are dynamically evolving, which could be associated with cognitive, behavioral developments during maturation and pathophysiology of brain disorders (Deco et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Deco et al., 2011.

claim: Using metabolic connectivity analysis, the components showing strengthened connections and at the same time enhanced connection efficiencies could be localized.
source: In this investigation using metabolic connectivity analysis, we could localize the components, that is, medial prefrontal and retrosplenial areas, showing strengthened connections and at the same time enhanced connection efficiencies.
evidence: This is supported by the combined results of connectivity and efficiency analyses shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Cognitive developments demand highly connected functional brain networks, particularly in hub regions.
source: Cognitive developments demand highly connected functional brain networks, particularly in hub regions (Micheloyannis et al., 2009; van den Heuvel and Sporns, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Micheloyannis et al., 2009; van den Heuvel and Sporns, 2013.

claim: Highly connected functional brain networks could accompany high-energy consumption in spite of limited supply of glucose for brain.
source: They could accompany high-energy consumption in spite of limited supply of glucose for brain (Smith et al., 2002; Tomasi et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Smith et al., 2002; Tomasi et al., 2013.

claim: The results of increased energy efficiency in retrosplenial and medial prefrontal cortex imply long-distance connectivity maturation coincide with the redistribution of energy consumption.
source: Our results of increased energy efficiency in retrosplenial and medial prefrontal cortex imply long-distance connectivity maturation coincide with the redistribution of energy consumption.
evidence: This is an inference based on the energy efficiency results shown in Figure 4.

claim: High-energy efficiency in hubs was previously reported in adult human brain.
source: High-energy efficiency in hubs was previously reported in adult human brain (Tomasi et al., 2013), which was recapitulated in our study in rats, and we also found that their high efficiency developed during brain maturation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Tomasi et al., 2013.

claim: High-energy efficiency in hubs was recapitulated in the study in rats.
source: High-energy efficiency in hubs was previously reported in adult human brain (Tomasi et al., 2013), which was recapitulated in our study in rats, and we also found that their high efficiency developed during brain maturation.
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: High efficiency in hub regions developed during brain maturation.
source: High-energy efficiency in hubs was previously reported in adult human brain (Tomasi et al., 2013), which was recapitulated in our study in rats, and we also found that their high efficiency developed during brain maturation.
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: Large-scale networks are formed during adolescent period accompanied by these networks' efficient energy consumption for long-distance connectivity.
source: Comprehensively, large-scale networks are formed during adolescent period accompanied by these networks' efficient energy consumption for long-distance connectivity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the combined results of the study.

claim: Deficits in the relationships between network formation and energy efficiency are found in several brain disorders.
source: As deficits in these relationships are found in several brain disorders (Broyd et al., 2009), metabolic network analyses might be used to find the relevant functional connectivity abnormalities.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Broyd et al., 2009.

claim: Metabolic network analyses might be used to find the relevant functional connectivity abnormalities in brain disorders.
source: As deficits in these relationships are found in several brain disorders (Broyd et al., 2009), metabolic network analyses might be used to find the relevant functional connectivity abnormalities.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of the methodology.

claim: The hub regions are well known as culprit components for several developmental and degenerative brain disorders.
source: Specifically, the hub regions are well known as culprit components for several developmental and degenerative brain disorders (Fornito et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Fornito et al., 2015.

claim: The results could explain the underlying biological background of the vulnerability that hub regions might be easily influenced by developmental problems in reconfiguration of metabolic connectivity efficiency.
source: Our results could explain the underlying biological background of the vulnerability that hub regions might be easily influenced by developmental problems in reconfiguration of metabolic connectivity efficiency.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the implications of the findings for understanding disease vulnerability.

claim: To find the disease-related abnormalities differentiated from normal developmental changes in neurological or psychiatric disorders, we need to characterize first the normal developmental patterns of metabolic networks.
source: To find the disease-related abnormalities differentiated from normal developmental changes in neurological or psychiatric disorders, we need to characterize first the normal developmental patterns of metabolic networks.
evidence: This is a statement about the rationale for the study.

claim: Metabolic networks have advantages to reveal steady-state connectivity in longer term scale than resting fMRI.
source: Although metabolic networks have advantages to reveal steady-state connectivity in longer term scale than resting fMRI, it is difficult to perform longitudinally repeated PET in the growing normal children.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the properties of metabolic networks and practical considerations.

claim: It is difficult to perform longitudinally repeated PET in the growing normal children.
source: Although metabolic networks have advantages to reveal steady-state connectivity in longer term scale than resting fMRI, it is difficult to perform longitudinally repeated PET in the growing normal children.
evidence: This is based on practical and ethical considerations of pediatric imaging.

claim: The findings in rats of maturational changes of metabolic connectivity can be referred to as surrogates, considering the homology between humans and rats in network components disclosed by ICA.
source: And thus, our findings in rats of maturational changes of metabolic connectivity can be referred to as surrogates, considering the homology between humans and rats in network components disclosed by ICA (Lu et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference about the translational relevance of the findings, supported by citations to Lu et al., 2012; Wehrl et al., 2013.

claim: Rat brains have similar features of metabolic network to human brains.
source: Although rat brains have similar features of metabolic network to human brains, there are several technical issues of interest.
evidence: This is supported by the ICA results and comparison with human studies.

claim: Rats should be anesthetized during either FDG injection or image acquisition.
source: Unlike human studies, rats should be anesthetized during either FDG injection or image acquisition.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental protocol.

claim: Anesthesia could affect brain metabolism.
source: Since anesthesia could affect brain metabolism, rats were awake after the injection until imaging to minimize the anesthesia effects.
evidence: This is established knowledge about anesthesia effects.

claim: Rats were awake after the injection until imaging to minimize the anesthesia effects.
source: Since anesthesia could affect brain metabolism, rats were awake after the injection until imaging to minimize the anesthesia effects.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used to address anesthesia effects.

claim: The images acquired from small animal PET had the voxel size of 0.3875 mm.
source: The images acquired from small animal PET had the voxel size of 0.3875 mm and physical spatial resolution of PET scanner is more than 1 mm due to positron range and acollinearity.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the imaging system.

claim: Physical spatial resolution of PET scanner is more than 1 mm due to positron range and acollinearity.
source: The images acquired from small animal PET had the voxel size of 0.3875 mm and physical spatial resolution of PET scanner is more than 1 mm due to positron range and acollinearity.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the imaging system based on physics of PET.

claim: Despite limited spatial resolution, the brain regions with specific covariance patterns were identified and metabolic connectivity analyses were feasible.
source: However, despite this limited spatial resolution, the brain regions with specific covariance patterns were identified and further metabolic connectivity analyses were finally feasible to provide characteristic pattern of brain maturation.
evidence: This is supported by the successful ICA and connectivity analyses presented in the study.

claim: Metabolic activity of rat brain matured to build connectivity between network components accompanied by enhanced energy efficiency from childhood to early adulthood.
source: We showed that metabolic activity of rat brain matured to build connectivity between network components accompanied by enhanced energy efficiency from childhood to early adulthood.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental results.

claim: Metabolism increased during adolescence in frontal cortices compared to childhood in rat brain similarly to that in human brain.
source: Metabolism increased during adolescence in frontal cortices compared to childhood in rat brain similarly to that in human brain.
evidence: This is supported by voxelwise comparison results and comparison with human literature.

claim: Components of metabolic networks were identified, and connectivity analysis showed efficient connection developed between the components particularly pair of VOIs including DMN during adolescent period.
source: Components of metabolic networks were identified, and connectivity analysis showed efficient connection developed between the components particularly pair of VOIs including DMN during adolescent period.
evidence: This is supported by ICA and connectivity analysis results shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The midline structures showed increase in energy efficiency of metabolic connections.
source: Furthermore, the midline structures showed increase in energy efficiency of metabolic connections.
evidence: This is supported by energy efficiency analysis results shown in Figure 4.

claim: This study about metabolic network maturation gave insights into normal brain developments.
source: This study about metabolic network maturation gave insights into normal brain developments and might elucidate the plausible pathophysiology of neuropsychiatric developmental diseases.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the study.

claim: This study might elucidate the plausible pathophysiology of neuropsychiatric developmental diseases.
source: This study about metabolic network maturation gave insights into normal brain developments and might elucidate the plausible pathophysiology of neuropsychiatric developmental diseases.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of the findings.

claim: Thirty adult male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were used for FDG PET scans.
source: Thirty adult male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats (Koatech, Seoul, Korea) were used for FDG PET scans.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.

claim: All the experimental procedures were approved by Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at Seoul National University Hospital (IACUC Number 13–0224).
source: All the experimental procedures were approved by Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at Seoul National University Hospital (IACUC Number 13–0224).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval.

claim: FDG PET images were acquired at the age of 5, 10, and 15 weeks.
source: FDG PET images were acquired at the age of 5, 10, and 15 weeks.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Rats were fasted for at least 8 hr before the start of the study.
source: Rats were fasted for at least 8 hr before the start of the study.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: After an intravenous bolus injection of FDG, each rat has 45 min period of FDG uptake.
source: After an intravenous bolus injection (0.3–0.5 mL/rat) of FDG (100–150 MBq/kg), each rat has 45 min period of FDG uptake (Schiffer et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol, supported by citation to Schiffer et al., 2007.

claim: Static scans at 45 min after the injection best reflects absolute rates of glucose metabolism in rodents.
source: Static scans at 45 min after the injection best reflects absolute rates of glucose metabolism in rodents (Schiffer et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Schiffer et al., 2007.

claim: During FDG uptake period, rats were awake for 35 min and anesthetized for preparation, 10 min before PET/CT scans.
source: During FDG uptake period, rats were awake for 35 min and anesthetized for preparation, 10 min before PET/CT scans.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: 88 PET images were acquired: 30 scans at 5 weeks, 30 scans at 10 weeks, and 28 scans at 15 weeks.
source: We acquired 88 PET images considering voxelwise statistical difference after multiple comparison correction: 30 scans at 5 weeks, 30 scans at 10 weeks, and 28 scans at 15 weeks.
evidence: This describes the sample size for the study.

claim: All brain PET images were spatially normalized to the FDG rat brain template using nonlinear registration on Statistical Parametric Mapping.
source: All brain PET images were spatially normalized to the FDG rat brain template (Schiffer et al., 2006) (PMOD 3.4, PMOD group, Zurich, Switzerland) using nonlinear registration on Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8, University College of London, London, UK).
evidence: This describes the image preprocessing methodology.

claim: The images were smoothened by Gaussian filter of 12 mm full width at half maximum.
source: The images were smoothened by Gaussian filter of 12 mm full width at half maximum.
evidence: This describes the image preprocessing methodology.

claim: The voxel counts were normalized to the global brain uptake in each PET image.
source: For scaling voxel intensities, the voxel counts were normalized to the global brain uptake in each PET image.
evidence: This describes the image preprocessing methodology.

claim: Paired t-test was performed between two groups of PET images acquired at 5 and 10 weeks.
source: Paired t-test was performed between two groups of PET images acquired at 5 and 10 weeks.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology.

claim: False discovery rate (FDR) corrected p < 0.05 was set as the significance threshold and an extent threshold of 100 contiguous voxels was applied.
source: False discovery rate (FDR) corrected p < 0.05 was set as the significance threshold and an extent threshold of 100 contiguous voxels was applied.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology.

claim: A group ICA algorithm was applied to define coherent network components.
source: We applied a group ICA algorithm to define coherent network components (GIFT, http://mialab.mrn.org/, GIFT ver 2.0a).
evidence: This describes the analysis methodology.

claim: All preprocessed PET images (n = 88) were included in spatial ICA to find spatially independent components and coherently activated regions among subjects.
source: All preprocessed PET images (n = 88) were included in this spatial ICA to find spatially independent components and coherently activated regions among subjects.
evidence: This describes the analysis methodology.

claim: The group ICA approaches have been used to obtain multivariate patterns for metabolic networks.
source: The group ICA approaches have been used to obtain multivariate patterns for metabolic networks (Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Toussaint et al., 2012; Yakushev et al., 2013.

claim: The optimal number of components extracted from PET images was determined using the dimensional estimation algorithm implemented in GIFT software.
source: Prior to perform ICA, the optimal number of components extracted from PET images was determined. We used the dimensional estimation algorithm implemented in GIFT software based on the assessment of entropy rate of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Gaussian random process (Li et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes the analysis methodology, supported by citations to Li et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2009.

claim: The estimated optimal number was thirteen components.
source: The estimated optimal number was thirteen components.
evidence: This is a result of the dimensional estimation analysis.

claim: ICA was performed using an infomax neural network algorithm that minimized the mutual information of the outputs.
source: ICA was performed using an infomax neural network algorithm that minimized the mutual information of the outputs.
evidence: This describes the analysis methodology.

claim: VOIs were placed on four ICs (IC1, IC5, IC8, and IC9) referring to rat brain atlas.
source: To compare the changes of brain metabolic connectivity according to age, we engaged VOI-based correlation analyses. VOIs were placed on four ICs (IC1, IC5, IC8, and IC9) referring to rat brain atlas, which was constructed on 3D digital map based on Paxinos and Watson atlas (Schiffer et al., 2006; Toga et al., 1995).
evidence: This describes the analysis methodology, supported by citations to Schiffer et al., 2006; Toga et al., 1995.

claim: These ICs were selected to concentrate on the relationship between functional components including DMN as intrinsically coherent regions at resting state and sensory-motor networks.
source: We selected these ICs to concentrate on the relationship between functional components including DMN as intrinsically coherent regions at resting state and sensory-motor networks.
evidence: This explains the rationale for IC selection.

claim: The total eight VOIs (3 on IC1, 1 on IC5, 2 on IC8 and IC9) were defined as spheres with a radius of 8 mm.
source: The total eight VOIs (3 on IC1, 1 on IC5, 2 on IC8 and IC9) were defined as spheres with a radius of 8 mm, centered at each IC (the actual size of a radius was 0.8 mm as voxels were scaled by a factor of 10).
evidence: This describes the VOI definition methodology.

claim: The size of VOI was determined considering initial voxel size and to a representative small cluster of a network not to overlap other networks.
source: The size of VOI was determined considering initial voxel size (0.775 mm) and to a representative small cluster of a network not to overlap other networks.
evidence: This explains the rationale for VOI size selection.

claim: Pearson's correlation coefficients were calculated between the pairwise VOIs using subjects variation.
source: We obtained normalized FDG uptake in the VOIs of each rat and Pearson's correlation coefficients were calculated between the pairwise VOIs (8x7/2= 28 paired VOIs) using subjects variation.
evidence: This describes the connectivity analysis methodology.

claim: Permutation tests were performed for statistical comparison of correlation matrices between groups of different ages.
source: For statistical comparison of correlation matrices between these groups of different ages, we performed permutation tests.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology.

claim: PET images of each age group were randomly permuted to make pseudo-random groups reassigned 10,000 times.
source: At first, PET images of each age group were randomly permuted to make pseudo-random groups reassigned 10,000 times and from each paired group of rats, interregional correlation matrices were calculated.
evidence: This describes the permutation test methodology.

claim: Type I errors were determined by the comparison between the observed Z score for each connection of VOI pairs and Z score distribution of VOI pairs from the permuted data.
source: Type I errors were determined by the comparison between the observed Z score for each connection of VOI pairs and Z score distribution of VOI pairs from the permuted data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology, illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: For multiple comparison correction, false-discovery rate (FDR) at a threshold of FDR < 0.05 was applied.
source: For multiple comparison correction, we applied false-discovery rate (FDR) at a threshold of FDR < 0.05.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology.

claim: Undirected networks with the eight nodes were constructed where strength of each connection was simply defined as correlation coefficients.
source: To analyze energy efficiency for metabolic connectivity, undirected networks with the eight nodes were constructed where strength of each connection was simply defined as correlation coefficients.
evidence: This describes the network construction methodology.

claim: Strength of metabolic connectivity was calculated for each VOI as a sum of weights of positive links per VOI.
source: Strength of metabolic connectivity was calculated for each VOI as a sum of weights of positive links (correlation coefficients) per VOI (Kaiser, 2011).
evidence: This describes the connectivity strength calculation methodology, supported by citation to Kaiser, 2011.

claim: The ratio of metabolic connectivity strength to normalized metabolic activity was defined as energy efficiency for each VOI.
source: The ratio of metabolic connectivity strength to normalized metabolic activity was defined as energy efficiency for each VOI (Tomasi et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the energy efficiency calculation methodology, supported by citation to Tomasi et al., 2013.

claim: Permutation tests were performed for statistical comparison of energy efficiency of VOIs between 5, 10, and 15 week-old rats.
source: For statistical comparison of energy efficiency of VOIs between 5, 10, and 15 week-old rats, we performed permutation tests.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology.

claim: The observed energy efficiency was compared with distribution of energy efficiency of each of VOIs from the permuted data.
source: The observed energy efficiency was compared with distribution of energy efficiency of each of VOIs from the permuted data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methodology, illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.
